newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan grains/oilseeds seen staying in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan grains/oilseeds seen staying in doldrums.

text.p: Taiwan's grains and oilseeds market is expected to remain in the doldrums this week as buyers continue to reduce their inventories following the outbreak of hog foot and month disease in March, traders said on Monday.
"We may not have a single tender for the entire week -- corn, soybeans or wheat," said one trader.
Trading has been thin since the government announced the epidemic on March 20 and ordered a pork export ban and island-wide drive to slaughter or inoculate 14 million hogs.
Grain traders have said Taiwan's 1997 corn imports would fall significantly from 1996 due to the epidemic, which sharply reduced demand for feed.
In recent weeks Taiwan importers have cancelled several corn tenders and at least one purchased shipment in the wake of the announcement as the mass hog slaughter slashed demand for corn.

In a Reuters Poll conducted on April 15, corn buyers and traders from six key grain firms all forecast that imports would fall sharply from 1996, when Taiwan bought about 6.5 million tonnes of corn, according to private estimates.
The poll forecast Taiwan's 1997 imports would range from just 4.9 million tonnes to 5.8 million tonnes and averaged about 5.19 million tonnes.
